translations.text: The beginning of the good news of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: “Look, I will send my messenger ahead of you, and he will prepare your way.
The voice of someone calling out in the wilderness: ‘Make the Lord’s way straight; make his paths straight.’”
John appeared, baptizing in the wilderness and proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
The whole region of Judea and all the people of Jerusalem went out to him. They were baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
John wore camel’s hair, with a leather belt tied around his waist, and ate locusts and wild honey.
He proclaimed, saying, “Someone stronger than I am is coming after me. I am not worthy to bend down and untie the strap of his sandal.
I have baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”
In those days Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized in the Jordan by John.
Immediately, as he was coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens opened and the Spirit coming down upon him like a dove.
And a voice came from heaven: “You are my beloved Son; I am pleased with you.”
Immediately the Spirit took him out into the wilderness.
He was in the wilderness for forty days, being tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals, and the angels served him.
After John was handed over, Jesus came to Galilee, proclaiming the good news of God,
saying, “The time has been fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near. Repent and believe in the good news.”
As he was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew, Simon’s brother, casting nets into the sea, for they were fishermen.
Jesus said to them, “Come, follow me, and I will make you fishermen who catch people.”
Immediately they left their nets and followed him.
When he had walked a little farther, he saw James the son of Zebedee and his brother John. They too were in the boat, preparing their nets.
Immediately he called them, and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers and went off to follow him.
They went into Capernaum, and immediately, on the Sabbath, he taught in the synagogue.
They were amazed at his teaching, for he taught them as someone who had authority, not as the scribes taught.
Immediately there was a man in the synagogue who had an unclean spirit, and he cried out,
saying, “What do you have to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are: you are the Holy One of God.”
Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silent and come out of him!”
The unclean spirit threw him to the ground, cried out with a loud voice, and came out of him.
They were all frightened, so they spoke to one another, saying, “What is this? Here is a new teaching with authority! He even commands the unclean spirits, and they obey him.”
News about him immediately spread everywhere throughout the surrounding region of Galilee.
Immediately after they came out of the synagogue, he went into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
Simon's mother-in-law was lying down with a fever, and they immediately spoke to him about her.
He approached her, took her hand, and raised her up. The fever left her, and she served them.
When evening came and the sun was setting, they brought him all who were sick and those who had demons.
The whole city gathered at the door of the house.
He healed many who were suffering from various illnesses and drove out many demons. He did not allow the demons to speak, because they knew him.
Very early in the morning, he got up and went out to a deserted place. He prayed there at that time.
Simon and those with him hurried out after him and found him.
They said to him, “Everyone is looking for you.”
He said to them, “Let us go somewhere else, to the other nearby towns, so that I may preach there too, for this is why I came out.”
He went throughout Galilee, preaching in their synagogues and also driving out demons.
And a man with leprosy came to him, begging him and saying, “If you are willing, you can make me clean.”
Moved with compassion, he stretched out his hand and touched him, saying to him, “I am willing. Be made clean.”
Immediately his leprosy left him, and he was made clean.
After giving him a strict command, he immediately sent him away.
He said to him, “See that you tell no one. Instead, go and show yourself to the priest, and offer what Moses commanded for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.”

But when he went out, he began proclaiming it widely and spreading the news, so that he could no longer enter the city openly. Instead, he stayed in deserted places, and people came to him from everywhere.
When he entered Capernaum after some days, people heard that he was in a house.
A crowd gathered there, so that there was not enough room for them even at the door. He spoke the word to them.
They brought a paralyzed man to him, carried by four men.

Because of the crowd, they could not bring him inside to him. They removed the roof above the place where he was, and after making an opening, they lowered the mat on which the paralyzed man was lying.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralyzed man, “My son, your sins will be forgiven.”
Now some of the scribes were sitting there, reasoning in their hearts.
“Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins except God alone?”
Immediately, when he perceived in his spirit that they were reasoning within themselves, he said to them, “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?”
For which is easier: to say to the paralyzed man, “Get up, pick up your mat, and walk,” or to say, “Your sins will be forgiven”?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins, he said to the paralyzed man,
“Get up, I tell you. Pick up your mat and go home.”
And he got up immediately, picked up his mat, and went out in front of them all. They were all amazed and gave glory to God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!”
He went out again beside the sea, and the whole crowd gathered around him, and he taught them.
As he was passing by, he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at his tax booth. He said to him, “Follow me.” And he got up and followed him.
While he was reclining at a meal in his house, many tax collectors and sinners reclined with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many of them, and they followed him.
When the scribes and the Pharisees saw that he was eating with sinners and tax collectors, they said to his disciples, “Why does he eat and drink with sinners and tax collectors?”
When Jesus heard this, he said to them, “Healthy people do not need a doctor, but sick people do. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”
John’s disciples and those of the Pharisees were fasting. They came to him and said, “Why do John’s disciples and the Pharisees’ disciples fast, but your disciples do not fast?”
Jesus said to them, “Can the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as the bridegroom is with them, they cannot fast.
But days are coming when the bridegroom will be taken away from them. Then they will fast in those days.
No one puts a patch of new cloth on an old garment. Otherwise, the new patch will pull away part of the old garment, and it will tear even more.
And no one puts new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise, the wine will burst the wineskins, the wine will spill out, and the wineskins will be ruined. Instead, new wine is put into new wineskins.”
On the Sabbath, he was walking through the planted fields, and as his disciples walked along, they began to pluck heads of grain.
The Pharisees said to him, “Look! Why are they doing what is not lawful to do on the Sabbath?”
He said to them, “Have you never read what David did when he and those with him were hungry?

How he entered the house of God when Abiathar was high priest and ate the bread of the Presence, which he was not permitted to eat, but only the priests, and also gave some to the others who were with him?”
He also said to them, “The Sabbath was made for people, and people were not made for the Sabbath.
So the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.”
He entered the synagogue again, and there was a man there whose hand was withered.
They were watching him closely to see whether he would heal the man on the Sabbath, so that they could accuse him.
He said to the man whose hand was withered, “Get up and come into the middle.”
And he said to them, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to kill it?” But they remained silent.
He looked around at them in anger, deeply saddened by the hardness of their hearts, and said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was healed.
When the Pharisees went out, they immediately plotted with the Herodians against him to destroy him.
Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea, and a large crowd from Galilee followed him, and from Judea
and Jerusalem. Another large crowd from Idumea, the far side of the Jordan, and the area around Tyre and Sidon heard what he was doing and came to him.
He told his disciples to keep boats ready for him because of the crowd, because they were pressing against him.
For he had healed many, so that they pushed toward him to touch him. And those who were afflicted with diseases
and the unclean spirits, whenever they saw him, would fall down at his feet and cry out, saying, “You are the Son of God!”
He sternly warned them not to make him known.
He went up the mountain and called those he wanted.
He chose twelve from among them, to whom he gave the [?] of apostles, so that they would be with him and he would send them out to preach
and give them authority to drive out demons.
And he appointed the twelve, and he gave Simon the name Peter.
And James the son of Zebedee and John the brother of James—he gave them the name Boanerges, which means “Sons of Thunder”—
and Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, and Simon the Cananaean,
and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed him.
He entered the house, and the crowd gathered around him again, so that they had no time to eat their bread.
When his family heard about it, they went out to take hold of him, for they were saying, “He is out of his mind.”
The scribes who had come from Jerusalem were saying, “Beelzebul is with him,” and, “He drives out demons by the ruler of the demons.”
Then he called them and spoke to them in parables, saying, “How can Satan drive out Satan?”
And if a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
And if a household is divided against itself, that household cannot stand.
And if Satan has risen against himself and is divided, he cannot stand, but his end has come.
But no one can enter a strong man’s house and steal his possessions without first tying up the strong man. Then he can plunder his house.
Truly I tell you, every sin and every blasphemy that human beings utter will be forgiven them.
But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never have forgiveness, but is guilty of an eternal sin.
This was because they were saying, “An unclean spirit is with him.”
His mother and his brothers came and stood outside. They sent word inside to him, calling him.
A crowd was sitting around him, and they said to them, “Look, your mother and your brothers are outside looking for you.”
He answered them, saying, “Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?”
He looked at those sitting around him and said, “Here are my mother and my brothers.”
“For whoever does the will of God is my brother and my sister and my mother.”
He began teaching again beside the sea, and a large crowd gathered around him, so that he got into the boat and sat in it on the sea. The whole crowd stood on the shore of the sea.
He taught them many things in parables, and in his teaching he said to them:
“Listen! Look, the sower went out to sow.”
“As he sowed, some seed fell beside the road, and the birds came and ate it.”
“Other seed fell on rocky ground, where there was not much soil. It sprouted immediately because there was not much soil beneath it.”
“When the sun rose, the plants were scorched, and because they had not put down roots, they dried up.”
Other seed fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked it, and it produced no fruit.
“Other seeds fell on good soil. They sprouted, grew, and produced a crop—thirty, sixty, and a hundred times as much.”
He said to them, “Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.”
When he had left the crowd, those with him, along with the Twelve, asked him about the parables.
He said to them, “The mystery of the kingdom of God has been given to you. But for those outside, everything will come to them in parables.”
So that, though they look, they may see and yet not perceive, and though they listen, they may hear and yet not understand, lest they turn back and be forgiven.
He said to them, “Do you not understand this parable? Then how will you understand all the other parables?”
“The sower sows the word.”
“These are the ones beside the road, where the word is sown: when they hear, Satan immediately comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.”
“Likewise, these are the ones sown on rocky ground: when they hear the word, they immediately receive it with joy.”
“But they have no root within them and last only a short time. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they immediately fall away.”
And others are those sown among the thorns: these are the ones who heard the word.
“The worries of this age, the deceitfulness of wealth, and the other desires that enter into them choke the word, and it produces no fruit.”
And those are the ones sown on the good soil: they hear the word, accept it, and produce fruit, thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.
He said to them, “Is a lamp brought in to be put under a measuring basket or under a bed? Is it not to be put on the lampstand?”
“For there is nothing concealed that will not be uncovered, nor anything hidden that will not be revealed.”
“Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.”
He said, “Pay attention to what you hear. The measure you use will be used to measure for you.”
“For whoever has will be given more, and whoever does not have, even what they have [?] will be taken away from them.”
He said to them, “This is what the kingdom of God is like: it is like a man who scatters his seed on his land.”
“He sleeps and gets up, night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows without his knowing.”
For the earth produces fruit by itself: first a blade, then an ear, and then a full grain in the ear.
But when the crop is ripe, he immediately brings the sickle, because the time for harvest has come.
And he said, “What shall I compare the kingdom of God to? Or what parable shall we use to describe it?”
“We shall compare it to a mustard seed. When it is sown in the ground, it is smaller than all the seeds on the earth.
But when it is sown, it grows up and becomes taller than all the garden plants, and puts out large branches, so that the birds of the sky can settle under its shade.”
And with all these kinds of parables he spoke the word to them, according to what they were able to hear.
He did not speak to them without a parable, but privately he explained everything to his disciples.
And on that day, when evening came, he said to them, “Let us go to the other shore.”
So they left the crowd and took him along in the boat, just as he was in it. Other boats accompanied him.
And a great windstorm arose, and the waves dashed against the boat, so that it was sinking.
But he was at the back of the boat, asleep on a cushion. They woke him and said to him, “Teacher, do you not care that we are going to die?”
He got up, rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Be quiet! Be silent!” And the wind stopped, and there was a great calm.
And he said to them, “Why are you afraid? Do you still have no faith?”
And they were filled with great fear and said to one another, “What kind of person is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”
And they went to the other shore of the sea, to the territory of the Gerasenes.
And when he stepped onto the shore, a man with an unclean spirit immediately met him, coming out of the tombs.
He lived among the tombs, and no one could bind him with a chain anymore.
For they had often bound him with shackles and chains, but he would tear apart the chains and break the shackles, and no one could overpower him.
And continually, night and day, he was among the tombs and in the mountains, crying out and being struck with stones.
When he saw Jesus from a distance, he ran, fell down at his feet, and worshiped him.
He cried out in a loud voice, saying, “What have you to do with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I adjure you by God: do not torment me!”
For Jesus was saying to him, “Come out of the man, you unclean spirit!”
And he asked him, “What is your name?” He said to him, “My name is Legion, because we are many.”
And they begged him earnestly not to drive them out of the territory.
Now a large herd of pigs was there at the foot of the mountain, being tended.
And they begged him, saying to him, “Send us into the pigs.”

And they allowed them to go. When the unclean spirits came out, they entered the pigs, and the herd of pigs rushed down the steep slope. There were about two thousand of them, and they died in the sea.
Those who were tending them ran away and reported it in the city and the countryside. People came out to see what had happened.
They came to Jesus and saw the demon-possessed man sitting down, wearing his clothes and in his right mind—the man who had had Legion in him. And they were afraid.
Those who had seen it told them what had happened to the demon-possessed man and about the pigs.
They begged him to leave their territory.
As he was about to board the boat, the man who had been demon-possessed begged him to let him follow him.
He did not allow him, but said to him, “Go home to your own people and tell them what the Lord has done for you,
and how he has had mercy on you.” So he went away and began proclaiming in the Decapolis what Jesus had done for him. And everyone was amazed.
When Jesus crossed over in the boat, he came to the shore. A large crowd gathered around him, and he was beside the sea.
One of the synagogue leaders, whose name was Jairus, came. When he saw him, he fell at his feet.
He begged him earnestly, saying, “My daughter is very ill. Please come and lay your hand on her so that she may be healed and live.”
He went with him, and a large crowd followed him and pressed against him.
There was a woman who had been bleeding for twelve years.
She had suffered greatly at the hands of many doctors and had spent everything she had. She had not improved at all, but had become worse.
When she heard about Jesus, she pushed her way into the crowd, came up behind him, and touched his robe.
For she said, “If I touch his clothes, I will be healed.”
Immediately the flow of her blood stopped, and she felt in her body that she had been healed of the affliction she had.
Jesus immediately realized within himself that power had gone out from him. He turned around in the crowd and said, “Who touched my clothes?”
His disciples said to him, “You see the crowd pressing against you, and yet you say, ‘Who touched me?’”
He looked around to see the woman who had done this.
The woman, frightened and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell at his feet and told him the whole truth.
He said to her, “My daughter, your faith has saved you. Go in peace and be healed of your affliction.”
While he was still speaking, people belonging to the synagogue leader came and said to him, “Your daughter has died. Why trouble the teacher any further?”
When Jesus heard the words being spoken, he said to the synagogue leader, “Do not be afraid; only believe.”
He did not allow anyone to follow him except Peter, James, and John, the brother of James.
They came to the synagogue leader’s house, and he saw them in an uproar, weeping and wailing loudly.
When he went inside, he said to them, “Why are you making an uproar and weeping? The little girl has not died but is sleeping.”
They laughed at him. But after he had put them all outside, he took the little girl’s father and mother and those who were with him and went into the place where the little girl was.
He took the little girl’s hand and said to her, “Talitha koum,” which means, “Little girl, I tell you, get up.”
Immediately the little girl got up and walked, for she was twelve years old. And immediately they were greatly amazed.
He gave them strict orders that no one should learn about this, and he ordered them to feed her.
He left that place and came to his hometown, and his disciples followed him.

When the Sabbath came, he began teaching in the synagogue. And the crowd, hearing him, was astonished and said, “Where did this man get these things? What is this wisdom that has been given to him? And what are these mighty miracles that this man performs?”
“Isn't this the carpenter, the son of Mary and the brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? Aren't his sisters here with us?” And they took offense at him.
Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not despised except in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own house.”
He performed no miracle there except that he laid his hand on a few sick people and healed them.
They were amazed at their unbelief. And he went around the villages, teaching.
He called the twelve and began sending them out two by two, and he gave them authority over unclean spirits.
He instructed them to take nothing with them for the journey except a staff—no bread, no bag, and no money in their belts.
Instead, they were to have sandals fastened to their feet and not wear two tunics.
He said to them, “Whatever house you enter, stay there until you leave that place.
And if a place does not welcome you and its people do not listen to you, shake off the dust beneath your feet as a testimony against them when you leave that place.”
They went out and preached that people should repent.
They drove out many demons, and they anointed many other sick people with oil and healed them.
King Herod heard about him, for his name had become well known. People were saying, “John the Baptist has risen from the dead, and that is why miraculous powers are at work in him.”
Others were saying, “He is Elijah.” Still others said, “He is a prophet, like one of the prophets.”
But when Herod heard, he said, “It is John, whom I beheaded. He has risen.”
For Herod had sent men to arrest John, bind him, and put him in prison because of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife, whom he had married.
For John had been telling Herod, “It is not lawful for you to take your brother’s wife.”
Herodias was angry with him and wanted to kill him, but she could not.
For Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and he honored him. When he listened to him, he was often astonished, and he listened to him gladly.
When a notable day came, Herod gave a banquet on his birthday for his high officials, military commanders, and the leading men of Galilee.
Herodias’s daughter came in and danced, pleasing Herod and those reclining at the meal. The king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”
And he promised her, “Whatever you ask me for, I will give you, up to half my kingdom.”
When she went out, she said to her mother, “What should I ask for?” Her mother said, “The head of John the Baptist.”
And she immediately went in to the king and asked him, saying, “I want you to give me the head of John the Baptist on a platter right now.”
And although the king was distressed, because of his oaths and those reclining at the table with him, he did not want to refuse her.
And immediately the king sent an executioner and ordered him to bring his head. He went and cut off his head in the prison.
He brought it on the platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.
And when the disciples heard, they came and took his body and laid it in a tomb.
The apostles gathered around Jesus and told him, reporting everything they had done and everything they had taught.
Then Jesus said to them, “Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a little.” For many people were coming and going, and they did not leave them time to eat.
And they got into the boat and went by themselves to a deserted place.
But many saw them leaving and recognized them. They came out of the towns and ran to where they were going, arriving ahead of them.
And when he came out, he saw a large crowd and had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd over them. And he began to teach them many things.
When it grew late, his disciples approached him and said to him, “This place is deserted, and it is already late.
Send them away so that they can go to the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves something to eat.”
But he answered them, saying, “You give them something to eat.” They said to him, “Shall we go and buy twelve hundred loaves of bread and give them to them to eat?” But he said to them,
“How many loaves do you have? Go and see.” And when they found out, they said to him, “Five, and two fish.”
And he ordered them to have everyone sit down in groups on the green grass.
And they sat down in groups of a hundred and groups of fifty.

When he took the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up to heaven and blessed them. He broke the loaves and gave them to his disciples to set before the people. He also divided the two fish among them all.
And they all ate and were satisfied.
And they picked up twelve baskets full of broken pieces, and they also picked up some of the fish.
Those who had eaten were about five thousand men.
And immediately he made his disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other shore, to Bethsaida, while he sent the crowd away.
And after he had said goodbye to them, he went up the mountain to pray.
When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was alone on the shore.
When he saw them struggling to row, because the wind was against them, he came to them during the fourth watch of the night, walking on the sea. And he intended to pass by them.
But when they saw him walking on the sea, they thought he was a ghost and cried out.
For they all saw him and were troubled. But he immediately spoke to them, saying, “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”
And he got into the boat with them, and the wind stopped. They were utterly amazed.
For they had not understood about the loaves, but their hearts were hardened.
When they crossed to the other shore, they came to Gennesaret.
When they went ashore, people immediately recognized him.
And they ran throughout that whole region and began bringing those suffering from illnesses on beds to wherever they heard he was.
And wherever he entered villages, cities, or the countryside, they would lay the sick in the marketplaces and beg him to let them touch the hem of his garment. And those who touched him were healed.
The Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around him.
And when they saw some of his disciples eating their bread without having washed their hands—
For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands, holding to the tradition of the elders.

And when they come from the marketplace, they do not eat unless they sprinkle themselves. And there are all sorts of other practices they have received and hold to: washing cups, pitchers, and bronze vessels.
The Pharisees and the scribes asked him, “Why do your disciples not live according to the tradition of the elders, but eat their bread with defiled hands?”
But he said to them, “Isaiah rightly prophesied about you hypocrites, as it is written: ‘Pilate [?] honors me with his lips, but their heart is far from me.
They worship me in vain, teaching human commandments as doctrines.’
You have abandoned the commandment of God and hold to human tradition.”
And he said to them, “You are very good at rejecting the commandment of God so that you can keep your own tradition!
For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘Whoever speaks evil of his father or mother must be put to death.’
But you say that if someone tells his father or mother, ‘Whatever benefit you might receive from me is Corban’—that is, a gift—
then you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or mother.
You invalidate the word of God through your tradition, which you have handed down. And you do all sorts of other things like these.”
And he called the crowd again and said to them, “Listen to me, all of you, and understand.
Nothing outside a person that enters him can defile him. Rather, the things that come out of a person are what defile him.”
And after he left the crowd, he went into the house, and his disciples asked him about the parable.
But he said to them, “Are you also without understanding in these matters? Do you not understand that anything outside a person that enters him cannot defile him,
because it does not enter his heart, but his stomach, and goes out into the latrine, cleansing all foods?”
And he was saying, “What comes out of a person is what defiles that person.”
For from within, from people's hearts, come evil thoughts, sexual immorality, thefts,
murders, adulteries, greed, wickedness, indecency, envy, slander, pride, and foolishness.
All these evil things come from within and defile a person.
When he left that place, he went to the region of Tyre and Sidon. He entered a house and did not want anyone to know, but he could not remain hidden.
But immediately, when a woman whose daughter had an unclean spirit heard about him, she came and fell at his feet.
The woman was Greek, from Phoenicia in Syria. She begged him to drive the demon out of her daughter.
He said to her, “Let the children eat their fill first, for it is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs.”
But she answered him, “Yes, Lord, even the dogs eat the crumbs under the children's table.”
And he said to her, “Go. Because of what you have said, the demon has come out of your daughter.”
When she went home, she found her daughter lying on the bed, and the demon had left her.
Then he left the region of Tyre again and went through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, through the region of the Decapolis.
And they brought him a man who was deaf and unable to speak, and they begged him to lay his hand on him.
He took him away from the crowd and led him aside. He put his fingers into the man's ears, and after spitting into his mouth, he touched his tongue.
And looking up to heaven, he sighed and said to him, “Ephphatha,” which means “Open.”
And his ears opened, the bond on his tongue was loosened, and he spoke clearly.
And he ordered them not to tell anyone. But the more he ordered them, the more they spread the news about him.
And they were utterly amazed, saying, “He has done everything well. He even makes the deaf hear and those unable to speak talk.”
In those days, a large crowd was with him again, and they had nothing to eat. He called his disciples and said to them,
“I have compassion for the crowd, because they have already stayed with me for three days and have nothing to eat.
And if I send them away without eating, they will faint on the road. Some of them live far away.”
His disciples answered him, “Who can provide enough bread to satisfy these people here in a deserted place?”
And he asked them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said, “Seven.”

And he ordered the crowd to sit down on the ground. He took the seven loaves, gave thanks for them, broke them, and gave them to his disciples to set before the people. And they set them before the crowd. They also had
a few small fish. After blessing them, he ordered these also to be set before the people.
They ate and were satisfied, and they picked up the leftover pieces, enough to fill seven baskets.
There were about four thousand people, and he sent them away.
Immediately he got into the boat with his disciples and came to the region of Dalmanutha.
The Pharisees came out and began arguing with him, asking him for a sign from heaven to test him.
And he sighed deeply in his spirit and said, “Why does this generation seek a sign? Truly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.”
He left them, got into the boat again, and went to the other side.
They had forgotten to bring bread with them, and they had only one loaf in the boat.
He warned them, saying, “Watch out! Be on your guard against the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod.”
They discussed among themselves the fact that they had no bread.
When he realized this, he said to them, “Why are you discussing the fact that you have no bread? Do you not understand or grasp it? Are your hearts closed?
You have eyes, but do you not see? You have ears, but do you not hear? And do you not remember?
“When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand people, how many baskets full of pieces did you pick up?” They said to him, “Twelve.”
When I also broke the seven loaves for the four thousand people, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you pick up?” They said to him, “Seven.”
He said to them, “How, then, do you still not understand?”
They came to Bethsaida, and people brought a blind man to him and begged him to touch him.
He took the blind man by the hand and led him outside the village. He spat into his eyes, laid his hand on him, and asked him, “What do you see?”
He looked up and said, “I see people walking around like trees.”
Again he laid his hand on the man's eyes. His sight was restored, he could see, and he saw everything clearly.
He sent him home, saying to him, “Do not go into the village.”
Jesus went out with his disciples to the villages of Caesarea Philippi. On the way, he asked his disciples, “Who do people say I am?”
They said to him, “Some say John the Baptist; others, Elijah; and others, one of the prophets.”
He asked them, “But who do you say I am?” Peter answered him, “You are the Christ.”
He sternly ordered them not to tell anyone about him.
And he began to explain to them that the Son of Man would suffer many things, be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, be killed, and rise after three days.
He was speaking openly about this. Peter approached him and began to rebuke him.
But he turned, looked at his disciples, and rebuked Peter, saying to him, “Get behind me, Satan! You are not thinking about the things of God, but about the things of human beings.”
He called the crowd together with his disciples and said to them, “Whoever wants to follow me must deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake and for the gospel will save it.
For what will it profit a person to gain the whole world and lose his life?
And what will a person give in exchange for his life?”
For whoever is ashamed of me and what is mine in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when he comes in his Father’s glory with the holy angels.
And he said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, some of those standing here will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God having come with power.”
And after six days, Jesus took Peter, James, and John and led them up a high mountain by themselves. And he was transformed before them.
And his clothes shone, becoming extremely white, whiter than any launderer on earth could make them.
And Elijah appeared to them with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus.
Peter responded, saying to Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to stay here. Let us make three shelters: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
For he did not know what to say, because fear had seized them.
And a cloud spread over them, and a voice came out of the cloud: “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him.”
And suddenly, when they looked up, they saw no one else with them except Jesus alone.
As they were coming down from the mountain, he commanded them not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
And they asked him, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
He said to them, “Elijah, when he comes, will indeed set everything right. And how is it written about the Son of Man that he must suffer many things and be treated with contempt?
But I tell you that Elijah too has come, and they did to him whatever they wanted, just as it is written about him.”
And when they came to the disciples, they saw a large crowd around them and some scribes arguing with them.
Immediately, when the whole crowd saw him, they were startled and ran to him to greet him.
He asked them, “What are you arguing about with one another?”
And someone from the crowd answered him, “Teacher, I brought my son to you. He has a spirit that makes him unable to speak.
And wherever it seizes him, it throws him to the ground, and he foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and becomes stiff. So I told your disciples to cast it out, but they could not cast it out.”
He answered them, “O faithless generation! How long will I be with you? How long will I put up with you? Bring him to me.”
And he brought the boy to him. When the unclean spirit saw him, it immediately threw the boy to the ground. After falling, he rolled around on the ground, foaming at the mouth.
He asked his father, “How long has this been happening to him?” He said, “Since his childhood.
And many times it has thrown him into fire and into water to kill him. But help us with whatever you can do, and have compassion on us.”
Jesus said to him, “You say, ‘Whatever you can do’? Everything is possible for the one who believes.”
Immediately the child’s father cried out, saying, “I believe! Help my unbelief!”

When Jesus saw that the crowd was running toward him, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, “Spirit that makes him unable to speak and hear, I command you: come out of him and never enter him again.”
After crying out and throwing him to the ground, it came out of him. He became like a dead person, so that many people said, “He has died.”
But Jesus took hold of his hand and raised him up, and he stood up.
When he went into the house, his disciples asked him privately, “Why could we not drive it out?”
He said to them, “This kind cannot be driven out except by prayer and fasting.”
When they left that place, they traveled through Galilee, and he did not want anyone to know.
For he was teaching his disciples, saying, “The Son of Man will be handed over to men, and they will kill him. After he dies, he will rise after three days.”
But they did not understand the saying, and they were afraid to ask him.
They came to Capernaum. When he went into the house, he asked them, “What were you discussing with one another on the road?”
But they remained silent, for on the road they had been discussing with one another who was the greatest among them.
He sat down, called the twelve, and said to them, “Whoever wants to be great among you must become less than everyone else and serve everyone.”
He took a little child and stood him in their midst. Then he put his arms around him and said to them,
“Whoever welcomes one of these little children in my name welcomes me. Whoever welcomes me does not welcome me but the one who sent me.”
John said to him, “Teacher, we saw someone driving out demons in your name, and we stopped him because he does not follow us.”
But Jesus said to them, “Do not stop him, for no one who performs a miracle in my name will be able to speak evil of me immediately afterward.
For whoever is not against us is for us.
For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink in my name because you belong to Christ—I tell you truly, he will not lose his reward.
And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck and he were thrown into the sea.
And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life maimed than to have two hands and go into hell, into the fire that cannot be put out.
And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to have two feet and be thrown into hell.
And if your eye causes you to sin, tear it out and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into Gehenna.
Where their worm will not die and their fire will not be put out.
For everyone will be salted with fire.
Salt is good, but if the salt becomes tasteless, what will you use to season it? Have salt within yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”
He left that place and came to the regions of Judea and the far side of the Jordan. The crowd gathered around him again, and, as he usually did, he taught them again.
They asked him, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?” They were testing him.
He answered them, “What did Moses command you?”
They said, “Moses allowed us to give them a certificate of divorce and send them away.”
But Jesus said to them, “Because of your hardness of heart, Moses wrote this commandment for you.”
But from the beginning of his creation, he made them male and female.
For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and join himself to his wife,
and the two will become one flesh.
Therefore, what God has made one, no human being should separate.
And when he went into the house, the disciples asked him again about this matter.
And he said to them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery against her.
And if she herself leaves her husband and marries another man, she commits adultery.”
And they brought little children to him so that he would lay his hand on them, but the disciples rebuked them.
But when Jesus saw this, he became angry and said to them, “Let the little children come to me, and do not rebuke them, for the kingdom of God belongs to those who are like them.
Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.”
And he took them in his arms and blessed them, laying his hand on them.
And when he went out onto the road, someone ran up, knelt before him, and asked him, “Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
But Jesus said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.
You know the commandments: Do not murder; do not commit adultery; do not steal; do not give false testimony; do not defraud; honor your father and mother.”
But he said to him, “Teacher, I have kept all these since my youth.”

But Jesus looked at him, loved him, and said to him, “You lack one more thing. Go, sell what you own and give it to the poor, and you will store up treasure for yourself in heaven. Then come and follow me.”
But he became gloomy at these words and went away grieving, for he had many possessions.
And Jesus looked around and said to his disciples, “It is difficult for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God.”
But the disciples were troubled by his words. Jesus answered again, saying to them, “My children, why is it difficult for them to enter the kingdom of God?
It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a sewing needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”
But they were even more astonished, saying to him, “Then who can be saved?”
But Jesus looked at them and said to them, “For human beings this cannot happen, but not for God, for everything is possible with God.”
Then Peter began to say to him, “Look, we have left everything behind and followed you.”
But Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, there is no one who has left a house or brother or sister or mother or father or child or field for my sake and for the sake of the good news
who will not receive a hundred times as much now, in this time—houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and fields, along with persecutions—and eternal life in the age to come.
But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.”
They were walking along the road, going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was ahead of them. Those following him were afraid. He called the twelve again and began to tell them what would happen to him.
“Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes. They will condemn him to death and hand him over to the Gentiles.
They will mock him, spit in his face, whip him, and kill him. And after three days he will rise.”
James and John, the two sons of Zebedee, came up to him and said, “Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask you.”
He said to them, “What do you want me to do for you?”
They said to him, “Grant us that one of us may sit at your right and the other at your left in your glory.”
Jesus said to them, “You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup that I am going to drink? Can you receive the baptism with which I am going to be baptized?”
They said to him, “Yes.” Jesus said to them, “You will indeed drink the cup that I am going to drink, and you will receive the baptism that I am going to receive.”
But to sit at my right or at my left is not mine to grant. It is for others for whom it has been prepared.
When the ten heard this, they began to be angry with James and John.
Jesus called them and said to them, “You know that those who say they are rulers of the Gentiles act as their masters, and their great men exercise authority over them.
But that is not how it is among you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must serve you.
And whoever wants to be first among you must be the slave of you all.
For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
As he was leaving Jericho with his disciples and a large crowd, Bartimaeus, a blind man, the son of Timaeus, was sitting beside the road begging.
When he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to shout, saying, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Many people rebuked him, telling him to be quiet. But he shouted all the more, saying, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Jesus stopped and instructed them to call him. They called the blind man, saying to him, “Take courage! Get up! He is calling you.”
He threw off his clothes, got up immediately, and came to Jesus.
Jesus responded to him, saying, “What do you want me to do for you?” The blind man said to him, “My teacher, I want to see.”
And Jesus said to him, “Go; your faith has saved you.” Immediately he could see, and he followed him along the road.
When they approached Jerusalem, at Bethphage and Bethany, near the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples.
He said to them, “Go to the village in front of you. As soon as you enter it, you will find a colt tied up, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it.
If anyone says to you, ‘What are you going to do with this?’ say, ‘The Lord needs it, and he will send it back here immediately.’”
They went and found the colt tied to a door in the street, and they untied it.
Some of those standing there said to them, “What are you doing, untying the colt?”
They spoke to them as Jesus had told them, and they let them go.
They brought the colt to Jesus and spread their clothes over it, and he sat on it.
Many others also spread their clothes on the road, while others cut branches in the fields.
Those going ahead of him and those following him were shouting, “Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!”
“Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest!”
He entered Jerusalem and went into the temple. After looking around the whole place, he went out to Bethany with the Twelve, since evening had already come.
The next day, when they came out of Bethany, he was hungry.

When he saw a fig tree in the distance with leaves on it, he went over to it to see whether he might find anything on it. When he came to it, he found nothing on it except leaves, for it was not the season for figs.
He said to it, “From now on, let no one eat fruit from you.” And his disciples were listening.
They entered Jerusalem. When he went into the temple, he began driving out those selling and buying in the temple. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.
He did not allow anyone to carry anything out of the temple.
And he was teaching them, saying, “Is it not written, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations’? But you have made it a den of robbers.”
The chief priests and the scribes heard this and looked for a way to kill him. They were afraid of him, because the whole crowd was amazed at his teaching.
When evening came, he went outside the city.
As they passed by in the morning, they saw that the fig tree had dried up from its roots.
Peter remembered and said to him, “Rabbi, look at the fig tree you cursed! It has dried up.”
Jesus answered them, “Have faith in God.”
“Truly I tell you, whoever says to this mountain, ‘Move and go into the sea,’ and does not doubt in his heart but believes that what he says will happen for him.”
“That is why I tell you: whatever you pray for and ask for, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.”
“Whenever you stand praying, forgive whatever you have against anyone, so that your Father in heaven may also forgive your sins.”
They came again to Jerusalem. As he was walking in the temple, the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders approached him.
They said to him, “By what authority are you doing these things? Or who gave you this authority to do these things?”
Jesus said to them, “I too will ask you a question. Answer me [?], and I too will tell you by what authority I do these things.”
“Where did John's baptism come from? Was it from heaven or from people? Tell me.”
They discussed it among themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘It was from heaven,’ he will say to us, ‘Why did you not believe him?’”
“But shall we say, ‘It was from people’?” They were afraid of the crowd, because everyone truly regarded John as a prophet.
They answered Jesus, “We do not know.” Jesus said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
He began to speak to them in parables: “A man planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a winepress in it, and built a tower. He entrusted it to tenant farmers and went away.
At harvest time he sent a servant to the tenant farmers to receive from them some of the vineyard’s fruit.
They seized him, beat him, and sent him away without giving him anything.
He sent another servant to them again. They killed that one too and treated him shamefully.
He sent another, and they killed that one too, as well as many others, beating some and killing others.
He still had a beloved son. He sent him to them after the others, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’
But those tenant farmers said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
They seized him, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.
What will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the tenant farmers and give the vineyard to others.
Have you not read this scripture either: ‘The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
This came about through the Lord, and it is a wonder in your eyes’?”
They wanted to seize him, but they were afraid of the crowd, for they understood that he had told this parable about them. So they left him and went away.
The Pharisees and the Herodians sent some people to him to trap him in something he said.

When they approached him, they said to him, “Teacher, we know that you are truthful and are not intimidated by anyone, for you do not show favoritism to people, but teach God’s way truthfully. Is it lawful to pay tax to the emperor or not? Should we pay or not?”
But knowing their hypocrisy, he said to them, “Why are you testing me? Bring me a stater coin so that I can look at it.”
They held it out to him, and he said to them, “Whose image and inscription are these?” They said to him, “The emperor’s.”
Jesus said to them, “Then give the emperor what belongs to the emperor, and God what belongs to God.” And they marveled at him.
The Sadducees, who say that there will be no resurrection, came to him and questioned him, saying,
“Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if someone’s brother dies and leaves a wife but leaves no child, his brother must marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
There were seven brothers. The first married a woman and died without leaving offspring.
The second married her and died without leaving offspring, and the third did likewise.
And so it continued through the seventh, without any of them leaving offspring. The woman also died.
In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be? For all seven lived with her.”
Jesus said to them, “Is this not why you are mistaken, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God?
For when they rise from the dead, they will neither take wives nor take husbands, but they will be like the angels in heaven.
But concerning the dead, that they will rise, have you not read in the book of Moses how God spoke to him at the bush, saying, “I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob”?
He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are greatly mistaken.
And one of the scribes came up to him, having heard them arguing and knowing that he had answered them well. He asked him, “Which commandment is the first of them all?”
Jesus answered, saying, “The first is: ‘Listen, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.'
And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.
And the second is this: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”
The scribe said to him, “Well said, Teacher. You have truly said that God is one and there is no other besides him.
And to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all your strength, and to love one's neighbor as oneself, is greater than all the burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
And when Jesus saw that he had answered wisely, he said to him, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” And no one dared to question him anymore.
And Jesus spoke while teaching in the temple, saying, “How do the scribes say that the Christ is David's son?
David himself said by the Holy Spirit, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies under your feet.”’
David himself says that he is Lord, so how is he his son?” And the whole crowd listened to him gladly.
And in his teaching he said to them, “Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in robes and love greetings in the marketplaces,
and the seats of honor in the synagogues, and the places of honor at dinners.
They devour widows' houses and make long prayers as a pretense. These receive greater condemnation.”
And when he sat down opposite the treasury, he watched how the crowd put money into the treasury. And many rich people were putting large amounts into it.
Then a poor widow came and put two small coins into it, worth one quadrans.
And he called his disciples and said to them, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put more into the treasury than all those who are putting money in.
For they all put in money from their surplus, but she, out of her poverty, gave everything she had to live on.”
And as he was leaving the temple, one of his disciples said to him, “Teacher, look at these stones—what stones they are! And these buildings!”
And Jesus said to him, “Do you not see these great buildings? They will not leave a stone upon a stone here without tearing them down.”
And as he sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew asked him,
“Tell us, when will these things happen, and what will be the sign when all these things are about to be fulfilled?”
And Jesus began to say to them, “Be careful that no one leads you astray.
For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and they will lead many astray.
But when you hear of wars and rumors of wars, do not be alarmed. These things must happen, but the end has not yet come.
Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines. These things are the beginning of the birth pains.

But be on your guard. They will hand you over to councils and beat you in synagogues, and they will bring you before governors and kings because of me, as a testimony to them and to the other nations.
And they will first [?] proclaim the good news.
And when they take you away to hand you over, do not worry about what you will say. Instead, say whatever is given to you to speak at that moment, for it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.
A brother will hand over his brother to death, and a father will hand over his child. Children will rise against their parents and kill them.
Everyone will hate you because of my name. But whoever endures to the end will be saved.
But when you see the abomination of desolation standing where it should not be—let the reader understand—then let those in Judea flee to the mountains.
Let the person on the roof not come down or go inside to take anything from his house.
And let the person in the field not turn back to take his cloak.
But woe to those who are pregnant and those who are nursing in those days!
Pray that your flight does not take place in winter.
For those days will be a time of suffering unlike anything that has happened from the beginning of the creation that God created until now, and nothing like it will ever happen again.
And if the Lord had not shortened the days, no one would survive. But because of the chosen ones whom he chose, he shortened the days.
And if anyone says to you, 'Look, the Christ is here!' or 'Look, he is there!' do not believe it.
For false messiahs and false prophets will arise and give signs and wonders to deceive the chosen ones, if they can.
But be on your guard. I have told you everything in advance.
But in those days, after that suffering, the sun will grow dark, and the moon will not give its light.
The stars will fall from the sky, and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.
Then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with great power and glory.
Then he will send his angels and gather his chosen ones from the four winds, from the farthest end of the earth to the farthest end of heaven.
Learn the lesson from the fig tree: when its branch has already become tender and its leaves sprout, you know that summer is near.
It is the same with you: when you see all these things happening, you will know that he is near, at the doors.
Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
But no one knows about that day or hour, neither the angels in heaven nor the Son, but only the Father.
Be on your guard, stay awake, and pray, for you do not know when the time will come.
It is like a man going away on a journey: he left his house and gave authority to his servants, assigning each one his work, and commanded the doorkeeper to stay awake.
So you too must stay alert, for you do not know at what time the master of the house is coming—whether in the evening, at midnight, when the rooster crows, or in the morning.
Otherwise, he may come suddenly and find you asleep.
What I say to you, I say to everyone: Stay alert.
Now the Passover and the day of Unleavened Bread were to take place in two days. The chief priests and the scribes were looking for a way to seize him by deceit and kill him.
But they said, “Not during the festival, so that there will not be an uproar among the people.”

While Jesus was in Bethany, reclining at the table in the house of Simon the leper, a woman came with an alabaster jar of perfume made from choice nard, which was very expensive. She broke the alabaster jar and poured it over his head.
But some became indignant, saying to one another, “Why was this perfume wasted?
For it could have been sold for more than three hundred staters, and the money given to the poor.” And they were angry with her.
But Jesus said to them, “Leave her alone. Why are you troubling her? She has done a good thing for me.
For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you wish, you can always do good to them. But I will not always remain with you.
She has done what she could. She has anointed my body with perfume beforehand for burial.
Truly I tell you, wherever this good news is proclaimed throughout the whole world, what this woman has done will be spoken of in remembrance of her.”
And Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests to hand him over to them.
When they heard this, they were glad and promised to give him money. And he looked for an opportunity to hand him over to them.
On the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they slaughtered the Passover sacrifice, his disciples said to him, “Where do you want us to go and prepare the Passover for you to eat?”
He sent two of his disciples, saying to them, “Go up into the city, and a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him.
Wherever he enters, say to the master of the house, ‘The teacher says: Where is my guest room, where I will eat the Passover with my disciples?’
He will show you a large upstairs room, furnished and ready. Prepare for us there.”
His disciples set out and went into the city. They found the place just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
When evening came, he arrived with his twelve.
While they were reclining at the table and eating, Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, one of you who are eating with me will betray me.”
They began to be distressed and to say to him one by one, “Is it me?”
He said to them, “It is one of the twelve, the one who will dip his hand with me into the bowl.”

For the Son of Man will indeed go just as it has been written about him. But woe to that man through whom the Son of Man will be betrayed! It would have been better for that man if he had not been born.
While they were eating, he took a loaf of bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “Take it. This is my body.”
And when he had taken a cup, he gave thanks over it and gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
And he said to them, “This is my blood of the covenant, which will be poured out for many.”
“Truly, I tell you, from this moment I will not drink the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.”
And after they had sung praise, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
And Jesus said to them, “You will all fall away, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’”
“But after I rise, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.”
But Peter said to him, “Even if they all fall away, I will not.”
Jesus said to them, “Truly, I tell you, today, this very night, before a rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.”
But he insisted at length, saying, “Even if I have to die with you, I will not deny you.” And all the other disciples said the same.
And they came to a field called Gethsemane, and he said to his disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”
And he took Peter, James, and John with him, and he began to be troubled and distressed.
And he said to them, “My soul is sorrowful to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch.”
And after going a little farther, he fell to the ground and prayed that, if possible, this hour might pass him by.
And he was saying, “Abba, Father, you can do anything. Let this cup pass me by, but not as I want.”
And he came and found them asleep, and he said to Peter, “Simon, are you sleeping? Could you not keep watch for a single hour?”
“Keep watch and pray so that you do not enter into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
And he went away again and prayed, saying the same words.
When he came to them again, he found them asleep, for their eyes were heavy, and they did not know what to say to him.
He came again for the third time and said to them, “Sleep now and rest. The matter has come to its conclusion. The hour has come. Look, the Son of Man will be handed over into the hands of sinners.”
Get up; let us go. Look, the one who will betray me has come near.
And immediately, while he was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, arrived, with a crowd carrying swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders.
Now the one who betrayed him had given them a sign: “The one I kiss is the man. Seize him and take him away securely.”
And when he arrived, he immediately went up to him, saying, “Greetings, Rabbi!” And he kissed him.
And they laid their hands on him and seized him.
But one of those standing there drew his sword, struck the high priest’s slave, and cut off his ear.
But Jesus answered them, saying, “Have you come out to arrest me as though I were a robber, with swords and clubs?”
“I was with you every day in the temple, teaching, and you did not seize me. But this is so that the Scriptures may be fulfilled.”
And they all left him and fled.
A young man was following him, wrapped in a linen cloth, and they seized him.
But he left the linen cloth behind with them and ran away naked.
They brought Jesus to the high priest, and all the chief priests, the elders, and the scribes gathered there.
Peter followed him at a distance, right into the high priest’s courtyard. He was sitting with the guards, warming himself by the fire.
The chief priests and the whole council were looking for testimony against Jesus so that they could put him to death, but they found none.
For many people gave false testimony against him, but their testimonies did not agree with one another.
But some stood up and testified falsely against him, saying:
“We heard him saying, ‘I will destroy this temple made by hands, and in three days I will build another not made by hands.’”
Even on these points, their testimony was not consistent.
The high priest stood up among them and questioned Jesus, saying to him, “Will you say nothing? What are these people testifying against you?”
But he remained silent and said nothing. The high priest questioned him again, saying to him, “Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”
Jesus said, “I am. And you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven.”
The chief priests tore their clothes, saying, “What other witnesses do we need?”
“You have heard the blasphemy he spoke. What do you think?” They all condemned him as deserving death.
Some began to spit in his face, cover his face, and strike him with their fists, saying to him, “Prophesy for us!” And the guards slapped him in the face.
While Peter was down in the courtyard, one of the high priest’s servant girls came.
When she saw Peter warming himself, she looked at his face and said to him, “You too were with Jesus the Nazarene.”
But he denied it, saying, “I do not know him, nor do I understand what you are saying.” And he went out to the entrance.
When the servant girl saw him, she said to those standing nearby, “This man is one of them.”
But he denied it again. A little later, those standing nearby said to Peter, “You really are one of them, for you are also a Galilean.”
But he began to curse and swear, “I do not know this man you are talking about.”
The rooster crowed a second time. Peter remembered what Jesus had said to him: “Before a rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.” And he began to weep.
When morning came, the chief priests, the elders, the scribes, and the whole council consulted together. They bound Jesus, took him away, and handed him over to Pilate.
Pilate asked him, “Are you the king of the Jews?” He answered him, “You are the one who says so.”
The chief priests accused him vehemently.
Pilate questioned him again: “Will you say nothing? Look how much they are testifying against you!”
But Jesus said nothing, so Pilate was amazed.
At the festival he would release one prisoner for them, whichever one they requested.
The man called Barabbas was imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder during the uprising.
When the crowd went up, they began to ask him to do as he usually did for them.
Pilate answered them, saying, “Do you want me to release the king of the Jews for you?”
For he knew that the chief priests had handed him over out of envy.
But the chief priests persuaded the crowd to ask him to release Barabbas for them.
Pilate answered them again, saying, “Tell me, then, what should I do with the king of the Jews?”
They shouted again, “Crucify him!”
But Pilate said to them, “What evil has he done?” But they shouted all the more, saying, “Crucify him!”
Pilate, wanting to satisfy the crowd, released Barabbas for them. But he had Jesus whipped and handed him over to be crucified.
The soldiers took him inside the courtyard, which is the Praetorium, and gathered the whole cohort around him.
They put a purple cloak on him, wove a crown of thorns, and placed it on his head.
They began to greet him, saying, “Hail, king of the Jews!”
They struck his head with a reed, spat in his face, and knelt before him and bowed down to him.
When they had finished mocking him, they stripped him of the purple cloak, put his own clothes on him, and led him out to crucify him.
They forced a passerby named Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the countryside, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry his cross.
And he brought him up to the place called Golgotha, which is translated “the place of the skull.”
They gave him wine mixed with gall, but he did not take it.
They crucified him and divided his clothes among themselves, casting lots for them to decide what each person would take.
It was the third hour when they crucified him.
The charge against him was written above him: “The king of the Jews.”
They crucified two robbers with him, one on his right and one on his left.
Those passing by insulted him, shaking their heads at him and saying, “Ha! You who will tear down the temple and build it in three days!
Come down from the cross and save yourself!”
Likewise, the chief priests were mocking him with the scribes, saying to one another, “He saved others, but he cannot save himself.
Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe in him.” Those who were crucified with him also insulted him.
When the sixth hour came, darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
At the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lama sachthanei,” which is translated, “My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?”
When some of those standing there heard this, they said, “Look, he is calling Elijah.”
Someone ran, filled a sponge with vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave him a drink, saying, “Wait! Let us see whether Elijah will come to take him down.”
Then Jesus gave a loud cry and gave up his spirit.
And the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
When the centurion standing opposite him saw that he had breathed his last [?], he said, “Truly, this man was the Son of God.”
There were also women standing at a distance, watching. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and Joses, and Salome.
These women had followed him since Galilee and served him, along with all the other women who had come up with him to Jerusalem.
When evening came, since it was the day of Preparation, that is, the day before the Sabbath,
Joseph of Arimathea came, a rich man who was a council member and who was himself waiting for the kingdom of God. He boldly went in to Pilate and asked him for the body of Jesus.
Pilate was surprised that he was already dead. He summoned the centurion and asked him whether it had been a long time since he died.
When he learned this from the centurion, he granted Joseph the body of Jesus.
Joseph bought a linen cloth, took the body down, wrapped it in the linen cloth, and laid it in his tomb, which had been cut out of the rock. And they rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.
Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses were watching where he was laid.
When the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices so that they could come and anoint him.
Very early on the first day of the week, they came to the tomb after the sun had risen.
They were saying to one another, “Who will remove the stone from the entrance of the tomb?”
But when they looked up, they saw that the stone had been removed, for it was very large.
When they entered the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on its right side, dressed in a white robe, and fear seized them.
He said to them, “Do not be afraid. You are looking for Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified. He has risen; he is not here. Look at the place where they laid him.
But go and tell his disciples, and Peter too, that he is going ahead of you to Galilee. You will see him there, just as he told you.”
They came out of the tomb and fled, for they were afraid and astonished. They said nothing to anyone, because they were afraid.

After he rose early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had driven out seven demons. [?] Tell them openly. After these things, Jesus also appeared to them again. From where the sun rises to where it sets, he sent out through them the holy and imperishable proclamation of eternal salvation. Amen.
She went and told those who had been with him, while they were mourning and weeping.
But when they heard that he was alive and that she had seen him, they did not believe.
After these things, he appeared in another form to two of them as they were walking, on their way into the countryside.
They too went and told the rest, but they did not believe them either.

Afterward, he appeared to the eleven themselves as they were reclining at the table. He rebuked their unbelief and their hard-heartedness, because they had not believed those who had seen him after he had risen.
And he said to them, “Go into the whole world and proclaim the good news to all creation.
Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned.
These signs will accompany those who believe: they will drive out demons in my name, and they will speak in tongues.
They will pick up snakes with their hands, and even if they drink a deadly poison, it will not harm them. They will lay their hands on the sick, and they will recover.”
After the Lord Jesus had spoken with them, he was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.
They went out and preached everywhere, while the Lord helped them and confirmed the message through the signs that accompanied them.
